The TUB Framework

Adam, Kelsey, and Tanya took The Uncommon Business (TUB) AI Bootcamp with Callan Faulkner. This is the shared language they came back with - a simple way to think about what AI can be and how built-up any AI tool is. Learn it and you'll understand the team's shorthand and be able to scope your own AI ideas.
For Staff - Intermediate

Framework by The Uncommon Business (Callan Faulkner). Summarized here as our internal team reference.

The Four Pillars of an AI-Powered Business

1AI-committed founder

Leadership that understands and invests in AI.

2AI architects

Every person becomes a builder of AI systems, not just IT.

3AI employees

The actual AI tools doing the repetitive work.

4AI business brain

The organized data, files, and context the AI employees draw from.

The Four Levels of an AI Employee
Each level adds one capability. The right level depends on the job - Level 4 is not always the goal.
LevelWhat it isWhat it addsWhen it's the right level
Level 1 - The ContractorA skill only, no company contextJust the capabilityOne-off tasks where context doesn't matter: grammar check, formatting, data transformation
Level 2 - The Trained EmployeeA skill + a brain (a project with context files)Company knowledge: tone, products, processAnything that needs to sound like School Tech or use our internal knowledge
Level 3 - The Connected EmployeeSkill + brain + connectorsReach into other tools (CRM, Slack, Sheets) to pull or pushWork that has to land somewhere after: update a record, post to a channel, log a result
Level 4 - The Autonomous EmployeeSkill + brain + connectors + a scheduleRuns on its own, no human triggerRepetitive, predictable, low-stakes recurring work: weekly reports, daily content, summaries
How the Levels map to our tools
  • A Level 1 Contractor is basically a skill on its own.
  • A Level 2 Trained Employee is a Project (the "brain" = a project loaded with STA context files).
  • Level 3 adds connectors (Gmail, Drive, Slack) - available in private Projects, or in Cowork.
  • Level 4 adds a schedule - that's Cowork's scheduled tasks (admins and power users).
New to chat vs Project vs Cowork? See that doc first.
The Four-Question Decision Tree
  1. What do you do repetitively that makes money but you don't enjoy? (finds the candidate task)
  2. Does this job need living context that changes over time? No = Level 1 is enough. Yes = build a brain (Level 2).
  3. Does it need to pull from or push into other tools? Yes = add connectors (Level 3).
  4. Should this run without you? Yes = put it on a schedule (Level 4). Test heavily before automating.
Principles the team quotes
  • "You cannot automate a process that does not exist." Define the manual version first; process before automation.
  • "AI reads transcripts top and bottom - the middle gets missed." Front-load what matters, use clear section markers, don't bury key details.
  • It takes roughly 40 to 60 hours of practice to get genuinely comfortable building AI systems.

TermWhat it means
AI architectA human who builds AI employees (Adam, Kelsey, and Tanya are AI architects)
AI employeeThe AI tool or system itself, not the human

SkillA reusable AI capability defined by a prompt or skill file
